{{Short description|British theoretical chemist}}

'''Patrick William Fowler''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is a British [[theoretical chemist]] known for his contributions to the understanding of molecular [[aromaticity]], [[fullerene chemistry]], and the application of [[graph theory]] to chemical problems. He is an Emeritus Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Sheffield]] and was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2012.<ref name="RS">{{cite web |title=Patrick Fowler FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/patrick-fowler-11455/ |website=Royal Society |access-date=2025-07-24}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Fowler was educated at the [[University of Sheffield]], where he completed his undergraduate and postgraduate studies in chemistry. After postdoctoral work and early academic appointments, he re-joined the Department of Chemistry at the University of Sheffield in 2005, where he spent the second half of his career.<ref>{{cite web |title=Emeritus Professor Patrick Fowler |url=https://sheffield.ac.uk/biosciences/people/emeritus-and-honorary-academics/patrick-fowler |website=University of Sheffield |date=17 February 2023 |access-date=2025-07-24}}</ref>

Fowler's work involves the application of mathematical methods, particularly graph theory, to problems in theoretical and [[computational chemistry]]. He has made contributions to the understanding of aromaticity, especially in polycyclic and non-benzenoid [[hydrocarbons]], and has applied symmetry and topology in elucidating the electronic properties of [[fullerenes]] and related molecules.<ref name="Fullerenes">{{cite book |last1=Fowler |first1=Patrick W. |last2=Manolopoulos |first2=D.E. |title=An Atlas of Fullerenes |year=1995 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=0198557876}}</ref>

He has authored or co-authored 600 peer-reviewed research papers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Patrick Fowler - Publications |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=zZ5awUkAAAAJ |website=Google Scholar |access-date=2025-07-24}}</ref>
